entries.test: Public evaluations and research available by May 5, 2024 would show whether reliability, reasoning, planning and hallucination problems remained unresolved despite substantial investment.
entries.note: “Failed to solve” strengthens “struggled to solve,” and the normalization omits the decades-long scope.
Neither the AGI endpoint nor “a long way to go” supplies a shared test.
Marcus endorses the uncertainty claim; the optimistic forecast inside the quotation is Altman's.

entries.test: Contemporaneous capability evaluations over the preceding fourteen months and public discussion of training-data constraints would test the reported stagnation and increasing concerns.
entries.note: The normalization replaces an observation about increasing concerns with a possibility claim and omits the other concerns.
“Within his grasp” has no shared capability or time threshold. The normalization drops the claims about evidence and engagement with critiques.
The central conclusion evaluates whether AI use is unequivocally great. The examples of existing harms could be checked separately.

entries.test: OpenAI's product revenue, expenditures and charitable activities through May 2024 would establish the relative scale of chatbot sales and charitable work.
Public licensing records, training-data evidence and reporting on Microsoft's profit-sharing agreement would test both the uncompensated use and contractual allocation claims.
entries.note: The normalization omits the specified first couple hundred billion dollars of profits. The profit clause describes an existing contractual arrangement.
Whether OpenAI has worked in creators' interests requires weighing benefits and harms without an agreed standard.
Marcus explicitly attributes this formulation to Dave Troy and adopts it. It denies a guaranteed connection rather than predicting failure.

entries.test: Public training-data licensing evidence and creator employment or commission records would test whether most affected creators were unpaid and many were losing work by May 2024.
entries.note: The rhetorical question presupposes nonpayment, and the following sentence directly asserts lost gigs.
“Basically following the same playbook” does not specify which combination of rhetorical practices qualifies.

entries.test: Release histories, comparative capability evaluations and published prices through May 5, 2024 would test the update, competitive-gap and pricing claims.
entries.note: The normalization drops “many,” the ongoing erosion of the gap, and the qualification that some prices are significantly lower.
“Likely” makes this probabilistic. Free availability is part of the predicted outcome, not an antecedent condition.

entries.test: Public evidence through May 2024 of durable advantages in technology, costs, exclusive assets or distribution beyond the existing customer base would test the absence of an evident moat.
entries.note: The plain business reading is an observable, durable competitive advantage.
Even if the stated legal conditions occur, “could” asserts only possible jeopardy.

entries.test: Public financial reporting through May 2024 and disclosed terms of Microsoft's agreement would establish historical net profitability and the required profit share.
entries.note: The future payments are presented as an existing contractual obligation.
“Maybe” qualifies the projected cost escalation.

entries.test: Consistent ChatGPT user or usage measurements from May 2023 through May 5, 2024 would show whether growth broadly plateaued.
entries.note: The observation ends at publication, not at the evaluation date.

entries.test: OpenAI's public demonstrations and contemporaneous independent capability evaluations through May 5, 2024 would test the absence of a demonstrated reliable agent and an apparent next-generation model.
entries.note: The agent clause is firm and publicly testable. The model clause is explicitly hedged and has a less precise capability threshold.
“Could conceivably” asserts possibility. The normalization resolves the ambiguous “there” into two explicit alternative targets.
“Selling hope” is a rhetorical characterization of the pitch.

entries.test: Public funding records and investor accounts of allocation decisions would test whether Altman's fundraising displaced funding for alternative AI approaches.
entries.note: The firm resource-diversion claim is testable; the environmental consequence is only possible. The normalization omits interpretability, reliability and diversion from broader humanitarian uses of capital.

entries.test: Subsequent investment records and public statements from people expressing belief in Altman's narrative would show whether they continued investing.
entries.note: The normalization narrows “people” to existing investors. No deadline is stated.
